item.title: Depth Delivers: UTEP men win in Cancun without top scorers
item.description: The UTEP men's basketball team has raved about its depth early in the 2026-27 season. On their first long road trip of the year at the Cancun Challenge against the College of Charleston, they got to live it. Playing in Mexico without their two leading scorers, Cam McDaniels and Youssouf Traore, who did not make the trip because of injuries, UTEP overcame the challenge and the now-4-2 Cougars, 80-69. The 5-1 Miners did it with a revamped lineup and depth, led by the most likely player, point guard Leif Moeller, and normal reserve Reid Cason. With the win, UTEP will play Eastern Michigan on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 6:30 p.m. MT. UTEP made this look fairly routine, taking control with a 12-2 run that helped stake the Miners to a 42-26 lead they saw home. In building the first-half lead that proved decisive, the Miners held Charleston to 19% shooting (1-of-14 from 3-point range) and held the Cougars without a field goal for the final 7:42 of the half. Charleston got going a bit in the second half, but UTEP had the margin it needed. UTEP was consistent offensively all game, finishing at 54% to Charleston’s 34%. The Miners didn’t blink down the stretch against the Cougars’ press to win their fifth consecutive game. As he was brought in to do, the sophomore Moeller was the glue with 14 points and 10 rebounds. Cason, getting his first start as a Miner, scored 12 points on 6-of-8 shooting and had six rebounds. Freshman Donovan Criss continued the impressive start to his UTEP career, scoring 13 points to go with three assists. UTEP won bench points 31-16 despite having two normal reserves, Cason and Jace Whiting, in the starting lineup. Where the Miners struggled was getting outscored at the free-throw line, as the Cougars were 29-of-37 to UTEP’s 15-of-20, as both Augusto Cassia and Cason fouled out as part of the Miners’ 27 fouls. The Miners won points off turnovers 18-11 despite giving the ball away 16 times to Charleston’s 14. Up next The Miners close the Cancun Challenge on Wednesday, Nov. 25 against either Eastern Michigan at 6:30 p.m. MT. It will be streamed on FloCollege and carried on 600 ESPN El Paso. item.title: Purdue basketball has to 'learn through failure' after latest loss to DePaul
item.description: FORT MYERS, Florida − This gauntlet was always going to give us a true evaluation of Purdue basketball and DePaul supplied valid documentation the Boilermakers have work to do. Just one game into a seven-game stretch against high major opponents, Purdue showed its flaws but also its fight. It resulted in a loss on Tuesday after the Boilermakers went the final 6:21 without making a field goal in a 65-56 loss at Suncoast Credit Union Arena. DePaul, one of college basketball's best early season success stories behind a rough and rugged physical defense, beat the Boilermakers black and blue. By the time Purdue attempted its first shot, the Boilers already had three turnovers. "I feel like we played hard for 40 minutes, but just not smart for 40 minutes," Purdue guard Gicarri Harris said. Purdue's ability to adapt will need to come quick. Over the next three weeks, the Boilermakers will see two of the eight teams with a higher defensive KenPom rating than DePaul. Iowa State (second in KenPom adjusted defensive efficiency) on Dec. 5 and Tennessee (fifth) on Dec. 11. The tough lessons learned in Tuesday's bare knuckle brawl might be what a team with some young guards who'd never faced that level of physical play before needs to see. More: Purdue basketball returns to cold shooting form in loss to DePaul Because, well, the Boilermakers play in the Big Ten, a league that also has six of KenPom's top 21 teams in adjusted defensive efficiency. Chris Holtmann has known Purdue coach Matt Painter a long time through their battles when Holtmann was head coach at Butler and Ohio State. He's seen this story before and what his Blue Demons team was able to utilize against Purdue on Tuesday will benefit the Boilermakers long term, he believes. "Defensively, we're a little bit unique, so I think Matt and his staff are one of the very best at having real month-to-month improvement with the program. ... " Holtmann said. item.title: Gilbert Arenas reveals how James Harden's influence is bigger than most people realize
item.description: Gilbert Arenas reveals how James Harden's influence is bigger than most people realize originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Now that James Harden is on the Cleveland Cavaliers , it looks like he is in decline, even if he has some promising games here and there. This is natural, of course, given his age and the 2026-27 season being his 18th year in the NBA. However, this has led to some people disrespecting him and his place in the record books. In fact, Harden is more influential than some people expect in the modern NBA. Even multi-time All-Star Gilbert Arenas agrees with the sentiment that Harden is one of the most influential players in the modern age. It may sound wild to some people, but Arenas is making a valid point there. Gilbert Arenas argues in favor of James Harden's massive influence on the modern NBA Despite his impressive legacy, it seems that Harden is still one of the players who gets regularly ridiculed in NBA circles. Even former players take some jabs at Harden, especially because of his struggles during the Playoffs. He has had tremendous regular seasons, but he can't seem to figure it out in the postseason. Yes, he has struggled during the Playoffs, but that should not erase all of his contributions. Arenas is one of the people who have not overlooked how influential Harden has been to the game. Not only has he brought the step-back to become a weapon that every star player has nowadays, but he has had an influence on the rest of the league. MORE: A Cavaliers insider reveals the root of James Harden's problems before the 2026-27 season Many modern stars have followed Harden's example of being a bigger guard who dominates the usage. The likes of Luka Doncic and Cade Cunningham come to mind as players who fit the mold. At the same time, Harden is also influential with moves like the step-back and the ability to generate free throws with smart drives to the paint. "James doesn't get the credit for being as smart as he is. You're talking about a guy who studied the game to the point where he used the rule book to his advantage. We can say what we want, but this NBA is James Harden's NBA. The shooting part of it and the threes are Steph's, but the NBA itself, this has been James Harden's NBA," Arenas said on his Gil's Arena show about Harden's influence . Harden is still in the NBA today, doing a lot of things that made him such a fantastic player during his prime with the Houston Rockets or even during his days with the Brooklyn Nets and Philadelphia 76ers . There are still glimpses from time to time that remind people of what Arenas is pointing out about influence. item.title: Florida basketball center Rueben Chinyelu’s historic day vs. Milwaukee puts him in rare SEC territory
item.description: [Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun] Florida basketball center Rueben Chinyelu’s historic day vs. Milwaukee puts him in rare SEC territory appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The No. 3 Florida Gators, who recently lost to the Houston Cougars , avoided getting upset by the Milwaukee Panthers on Tuesday at Tower Hill Arena in Gainesville, thanks in large part to the incredible night senior big man Rueben Chinyelu had. Chinyelu flexed his muscles and dominated the visiting Panthers, finishing with 25 points and 16 rebounds, while shooting 10-for-12 from the field, 1-for-1 from behind the arc and 4-for-4 from the free-throw line in 31 minutes of action. He added two blocks and an assist, as Florida basketball improved to 7-1 overall. With his stellar performance against Milwaukee, Chinyelu also put himself in an elite group of SEC players. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He’s just the second SEC player in 30 years with 25 PTS, 15 REB and 80% shooting in a game,” the official X (formerly Twitter) account of the SEC Network shared. It was quite a bounce-back showing from Chinyelu, who only appeared in 12 minutes in the previous Florida game against the West Virginia Mountaineers at home last Friday, scoring just two points with four rebounds and two assists before fouling out in an 85-72 victory. Chinyelu had actually produced minimally on offense in the three games before his eruption against Milwaukee, as he racked up just a total of 14 points on 5-for-11 shooting over that stretch. Chinyelu isn’t known for scoring as much as the toughness he brings inside and his ability to clean the glass for Florida , but it was great for the Gators to see him confidently get buckets on Tuesday. If anything, Chinyelu’s big night against the Panthers is a good momentum-builder for him as the Gators next take on the No. 16 Duke Blue Devils on Dec. 1 in Gainesville. item.title: Brian Kelly would be ‘surprised’ if SEC doesn’t give LSU the boot after RJ Luis controversy
item.description: Brian Kelly doesn’t see this ending well for LSU. SEC leadership is expecting to meet on Dec. 3, with the future of Kelly’s former employer up for debate . “This has gotten to the point where they will have a meeting on Dec. 3. The presidents will vote and I’ll actually be surprised if they don’t vote them out,” Kelly said in an appearance on SiriusXM’s “The Early Read” on Tuesday. Coach Brian Kelly of the LSU Tigers squats on the sideline during a 2025 game. Getty Images The Tigers have drawn the ire of their own conference in recent months by recruiting players who signed professional contracts for their football and basketball teams. Things came to a head when Will Wade’s men’s basketball team rostered and then played former St. John’s star RJ Luis in a game against UL Monroe on Nov. 18 — despite “numerous representations” that he wouldn’t take the court, according to the SEC. The following day, LSU president Wade Rousse told Wade not to play Luis , who spent time with the NBA’s Jazz and Celtics, but never got into any action. “They’ve asked them to come and meet them halfway a couple of times,” Kelly said. “I think the Luis situation and playing him in the game went against any kind of good faith that they had. I think this is going to go right down to a vote. College football and college athletics will all have to take notice with where we are and where we want to go.” Kelly, the Tigers’ former football coach, was famously fired eight games into his fourth season leading the team, with a 34-14 mark during his tenure. The move resulted in a $54 million payout and led to the hiring of Lane Kiffin — who opted not to put Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris on his roster this season despite speculation he’d find spots for the NFLers after they were granted an extra year of eligibility. The SEC officially passed a rule in August barring teams from rostering players who signed professional contracts in their respective sports, with commissioner Greg Sankey having authority to enforce penalties and sanctions. RJ Luis Jr. dribbles up court during LSU’s recent win over the ULM Warhawks. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect “I don’t have any firsthand information other than following it like you folks have, and knowing Greg Sankey and what they’re about,” Kelly said. “They wanna be able to present the SEC rules and regulations relative to how member institutions operate on a day-to-day basis. That hasn’t been followed. I think that they’ve reached that point where, you know what? We can’t keep bluffing. We’ve gotta make a decision here, and I think we’re gonna have some kind of decision, whether it’s terminating their membership or whether people are suspended, the SEC’s gonna act.”

item.title: Pistons down Magic, Celtics hold off Wizards
item.description: Detroit's Daniss Jenkins and Ausar Thompson combine to block Orlando's Anthony Black (Rich Storry) The Detroit Pistons shrugged off the injury absence of Cade Cunningham to keep their NBA Cup hopes alive on Tuesday with a gritty 104-86 road victory over the Orlando Magic. Isaiah Joe led Detroit's scoring with 21 points after nailing five three-pointers as five Pistons players finished in double figures. Orlando, who could have booked their place in the knockout rounds with a victory, started brightly to take a 22-16 lead after the first quarter. But a devastating scoring burst from Detroit in the second quarter, outscoring Orlando 32-14, changed the contest. Detroit took a 48-36 lead into half-time and maintained a double-digit cushion for most of the remainder of the game. "I thought our defense was elite tonight," Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff said. "On a night where we were down some offense, we knew we were going to have to hang our hat on the defensive end of the floor and I love the way that everybody contributed. "Everbody bought into it and that was the best part. We knew it was going to be a gritty, physical game, but our guys did a great job." Orlando lead the Eastern Conference Group A with a 3-1 record while the Pistons are in third place on 2-1 behind the Toronto Raptors. The Boston Celtics all but locked up their place in the quarter-finals after holding off a furious rally from the Washington Wizards to score a 131-116 win on the road in the East's Group C. Jayson Tatum scored 41 points for the Celtics while Paul George added 28 and Neemias Queta 21 to halt Boston's four-game losing streak. The Celtics looked to be cruising towards a crushing win after racing into a 34-point lead just before half-time. But the Wizards hit back to outscore Boston 40-24 in the third quarter and got to within seven points of the lead late in the fourth at 119-112. Boston regrouped down the stretch and a pair of three-pointers from Baylor Scheierman saw the Celtics pull clear. "We had a tough week last week for various different reasons," Tatum said of Boston's run of four straight losses before Tuesday. "But you can't change what happens. We always try to focus on today," he told NBC. Tatum added he was not surprised by the Wizards' rally. "No lead is safe and they get paid to play basketball too, right?" he said. "They’ve got a lot of talent over there so it was just a case of trying to weather the storm." rcw/pst

item.title: No. 1 South Carolina controls UConn again in rematch of dramatic Final Four showdown
item.description: UNCASVILLE, Conn. — Coming into the highly anticipated Final Four rematch Tuesday night between No. 1 South Carolina and No. 7 UConn, all eyes were on Dawn Staley and Geno Auriemma. Would they shake hands? Would they exchange pleasantries? Would their pregame meeting unravel into another clash? But by the end of the first quarter, any intrigue over how the Staley-Auriemma dynamic would play out in a rematch of last season’s Final Four blowup was nullified by Tessa Johnson. The Gamecocks guard scored a career-high 32 points to power South Carolina to a 65-56 win over UConn in the Women’s Basketball Hall of Fame Showcase. South Carolina (7-0) has put itself in a category of its own to start the season, with depth and firepower for which opponents have had no answers. Even without All-American forward Joyce Edwards, who was out with an illness, the Gamecocks proved again that they set the bar. The result wasn’t as stunning as last season’s 62-48 blowout of the Huskies in the Final Four, but South Carolina looked like the dominant team for most of the game. In the first quarter, UConn looked like a team worthy of sharing the same court. But by the midway point in the second quarter it had become clear that the Gamecocks had merely taken a bit to settle in. South Carolina closed the early gap by playing tighter defense and finding the bottom of the net. After shooting 3-for-16 in the first quarter, the Gamecocks went 9-of-23 in the second and forced seven UConn turnovers. Staley’s squad went into the half on a 22-2 run, including three consecutive 3-pointers to close out the second quarter. Two came from Johnson and the third from Agot Makeer, which she turned into a four-point play after drawing a foul on Sarah Strong. The Huskies (4-3) were led by Strong, who finished with 22 points and 11 rebounds. No one else scored in double figures for UConn. At first glance, the changes outlined by the governing bodies aim to limit distance gains for pro players with the driver and golf ball, but appear to fall short of the distance drops targeted by the golf ball rollback standard initially pursued back in 2023. But let’s hold on for a second. If you’re a golfer with a normal degree of exposure to governing body minutiae, you’ve probably got no idea what I just said. So let’s get you the goods without the headache in Q&A form. 1. What’s the backstory? The USGA and R&A have been looking to curb distance in pro golf for years … but as it turns out, it’s pretty hard to curb distance! Players hate it. Club companies hate it. Regular golfers hate it. The governing bodies don’t even seem to like it. In fact, it might be said that curbing distance in golf is a lot like eating chard — if it’s so good for you, why does it taste like that?! The USGA and R&A are unusual in that they are self-aware enough to recognize their chard-iness. They have tried very hard to find a solution to the distance problem that will satisfy everyone or, at least, annoy everyone the least. Ben Stokes has found his way into the IPL 2027 mini-auction even though he stayed away from the mega-auction that preceded the 2025 season, and the route he took has raised plenty of eyebrows. The former England Test captain, who is 35, has registered at the top base price of ₹2 crore for the event on December 16, 2026, in Goa. His name sits in an initial longlist of 1,220 players, and he is one of 30 marquee names who have put themselves in the ₹2 crore bracket. The surprise comes from the fact that Stokes did not sign up for the last mega-auction held in November 2024. He reportedly wanted to protect his workload and give priority to England's busy international schedule at the time, which was a reasonable call for a player carrying heavy responsibilities across formats. Under the rules the BCCI introduced before that mega-auction, a decision like his should have had consequences for the next cycle. That is why his registration for the mini-auction in the same cycle has left many followers asking how the league allowed it, and the answer lies in a rule, an exception and a change in his career. MORE: IPL 2027 auction alongside the player list, rules and date What the BCCI rule says about overseas players who skip the mega auction? The IPL Player Regulations made it compulsory for overseas players to take part in the mega auction if they wished to remain eligible later. The regulations state: "Any Overseas Player will have to register for the Big Auction." The rule then spells out the penalty, which is that an overseas player who does not register is barred from entering the subsequent mini-auctions in the same cycle. On paper, therefore, Stokes was meant to be out of the mini-auction pool. It is worth separating this regulation from a different one, because the two are often confused. The two-season ban applies only to players who register, are picked at an auction and then withdraw before the season begins, which is not what happened with Stokes. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
